column1: # §7.2 Ordinal + §7.3 Agreement — CLDR de RBNF %spellout-ordinal(-n/-r/-s/-m); Duden Grammatik agreement.
# Only in resolvable contexts: before a month name, before a lexicon noun, or in a numeric date.
# §7.3 row: der + N. + feminine noun -> weak dative/genitive -en, -n
# §7.3 row: seit/ab/bis/nach/vor + N. + month -> strong dative -em
# §7.3 row: bare N. + noun (no trigger) -> strong nominative by gender, -er/-e/-es
# negative: bare N. with no resolvable context is not an ordinal; the number reads as a Cardinal and the period stays (§9: no digits in output)
# negative: bare N. at sentence end with no month/lexicon noun following, same
# Inputs below marked "# text-processing-rs" are NeMo-derived TN test inputs from FluidInference/text-processing-rs (tests/fixtures/de, Apache-2.0); the expected outputs are ours.
# text-processing-rs: a weak trigger (am/vom/zum/beim/im/dem/den/des/die/das) fixes the ending for every gender, so no lexicon noun is needed
# negative: a strong trigger still needs a noun of known gender
# extrapolated: reaches the ordinal "ß" form ("dreißigste"), kept by default
# A determiner or preposition before N. and a lower-case adjective after it: the ordinal takes the adjective's ending (Duden Grammatik: successive attributive adjectives inflect alike).
# indefinite article: the adjective's ending, not a default
# closed-class words end like adjectives but do not carry the ordinal's ending: a gender-free trigger keeps its own
